Use Tier 3: add a SASRec sequential expert alongside the current LightGCN model and ensemble their predictions. The graph model captures collaborative preferences but compresses chronological history into a weighted average, losing order-dependent transitions. Electronics currently scores 0.34 HR@10 versus the SASRec baseline’s 0.42, while the graph model performs better on CDs_and_Vinyl, suggesting complementary strengths.

Modify model_design by retaining the current graph expert and adding one baseline SASRec expert per category, trained exclusively on the existing training sequences. Keep each expert’s architecture, sampling, and optimization otherwise unchanged so this experiment isolates the ensemble’s contribution. Combine their candidate scores using equal-weight reciprocal-rank fusion, which avoids assuming that their logit scales are comparable and requires no fitted blending parameters.

Modify training_evaluation to select each expert’s checkpoint using the fixed validation protocol, then compute the ensemble’s actual macro-average HR@10 across all four categories. Modify the predictor writer to load both trained experts for the requested dataset, apply identical history processing and fusion during validation and host inference, and return scores in the original candidate order. Preserve DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], training seed 42, all existing splits, and artifacts beneath the trial directory; cap training time per category to retain all four models within the run budget. Print the measured Final Validation Score, and leave held-out predictions to the host evaluator without accessing hidden test files or fabricating a submission.csv.
